board_name: Indiana Board of Pharmacy (Indiana Professional Licensing Agency)
refresh_cadence: not stated (generated on demand from the live PLA database)

notes: bulk_file=paid stands for a true file, but three claim fields are refuted outright. (1) retains_closed is YES, not unknown - Indiana carries an explicit 'Closed Facility' status alongside 'Expired' and returns both in free search results. (2) nonresident_included is YES - out-of-state facility rows (PA, WI, IL, CA, FL, OH) come back in the same search. (3) The 'JS-only per-record SPA' characterisation is wrong: the 5,806-byte page is a server-rendered form (Option 3 is literally 'Search by Facility Name (For facility or business entity certification (e.g. Pharmacy, Salon, Corporation)') and one POST of FacilityName=A returned 10,634 rows in a single 6.4 MB HTML page with no CAPTCHA and no paging. Practically, that makes Indiana enumerable for free at the summary level, though closure DATES are still unavailable - status is exposed without any dated event, and the free tier gives only Full Name / License # / License Type / License Status / City / State. The claim's fields_present (issue_date, expiration_date, address true) describes the PAID CSV product, which is a defensible reading, so I am leaving those flags alone.

board_name: State of Ohio Board of Pharmacy
bulk_url: https://www.pharmacy.ohio.gov/licensing/rosterrequests — ASP.NET form POST with ctl00$phBody$rblLicenseType=7 (Terminal Distributor) AND ctl00$phBody$rblLicenseStatus=2 (Active & Inactive), plus __VIEWSTATE/__VIEWSTATEGENERATOR/__EVENTVALIDATION and ctl00$phBody$btnSubmit=Download Data. The documented listid=7 URL returns the ACTIVE-ONLY subset.
refresh_cadence: live-on-demand — generated at request time, filename stamped with the current date
portal_type: Ohio eLicense (Salesforce-based license lookup)
notes: Missed by the earlier check. Ohio DOES retain closed licenses in bulk — the roster page has a 'License Status To Be Included' radio with an 'Active & Inactive Licenses' option that an earlier check never exercised, because the board's own instruction manual only documents the active-only listid URLs. Flipping it nearly triples the file (4.4 MB / 22,532 rows -> 11.3 MB / 63,108 rows) and exposes an explicit LicenseSubStatus column with Closed / Surrendered / Revocation / Lapsed values. Ohio therefore ranks with NJ and NV on closure retention, not with the active-only states. Still no closure DATE field, so closure_dated=no stands. Caveat: robots.txt on this host disallows /*?* (all query-string URLs), which covers the documented listid=7 link; the form POST path carries no query string.

board_name: Oklahoma State Board of Pharmacy
refresh_cadence: daily (page header showed "Last Updated: 8/15/2026 7:17:20 PM"); board states it "performs daily updates to the website"
portal_type: custom classic ASP / IIS (CodeCharge-generated "Clear" theme), no CAPTCHA, no JS required, GET-pageable
notes: Core claim Confirmed and if anything understated. Two corrections: (1) approx_rows is 9,544, not 9,555 — the portal prints an explicit "Total Records:  9544" in the list header, so an earlier check's 637 pages x 15 rows inference was wrong. (2) The scrape is far cheaper than "~637 list pages": the paginator is plain GET (PhrmcySearch.asp?tblPharmaciesPage=N) AND honors a page-size parameter — PhrmcySearch.asp?tblPharmaciesPageSize=100 returns 100 detail links in one response, so the full roster is ~96 GET pages, not 637. Also worth adding: each detail page carries a Disciplinary Action table (Case Date / Case Number), so per-record disciplinary history IS public even though license-status history is not; history_public="no" is defensible only if read strictly as status history.

board_name: Oregon Board of Pharmacy

board_name: Pennsylvania State Board of Pharmacy, Bureau of Professional and Occupational Affairs (Dept. of State)
refresh_cadence: stale — Socrata rowsUpdatedAt = 2025-07-01 14:53 UTC (last refreshed ~13 months ago); no stated cadence
portal_type: PALS — Pennsylvania Licensing System (AngularJS SPA + ASP.NET, ag-grid, Google reCAPTCHA v3 required per search)
notes: Correction on bulk file: An earlier check searched data.pa.gov's Socrata catalog only for q=license and so saw only the aggregate counts dataset (fwj2-whnj); searching q=pharmacy surfaces ysdx-4vmi "Find Naloxone at a Pharmacy Near Me Current Statewide Department of State and Health", which is a Department-of-State-sourced roster of 3,324 distinct PA pharmacy SITE license numbers with name and full street address — a bulk file of pharmacy facilities on a state open-data portal, which the brief says counts. Real caveats that keep this Tier 2-ish: it carries only licensenumber, fullname, addressline1, pcity, pstate, pzipcode, pcounty and a geocode — NO status, NO issue date, NO expiration date, NO closure date, NO owner/PIC; it is PA-addressed only (0 out-of-state rows, so nonresident pharmacies are NOT in it); it is a naloxone-standing-order/community-pharmacy view rather than the full facility roster (institutional and nonresident classes absent); and it has not been refreshed since 2025-07-01. The PALS half of the claim is otherwise Confirmed. Two smaller corrections to the evidence: the legacy page https://www.dos.pa.gov/ProfessionalLicensing/Pages/Licensing-Data.aspx returns HTTP 200 to curl and 302s (not 301s) via /Redirect to https://www.pa.gov/en/agencies/dos.html — either way no data-files page survives, so the conclusion stands.

board_name: Rhode Island Department of Health, Board of Pharmacy (Office of Health Professions Regulation)
refresh_cadence: Not stated on page; page footer read 'Last Updated on: Friday, 14th August 2026'. File content is a live extract of the RIDOH licensing DB.

board_name: South Carolina Board of Pharmacy (SC Dept. of Labor, Licensing & Regulation)
refresh_cadence: nightly — the lookup page states "This website is maintained by LLR staff and is updated nightly reflecting changes to our licensing and enforcement database." (the $10 mailed roster itself is produced on request)
portal_type: In-house LLR 'LicLookup' ASP.NET WebForms app (verify.llronline.com); not MyLicense/iGov/Accela/Salesforce
notes: Substance of the claim Confirmed — the $10 roster request and the anti-automation "Incorrect" gate both replicate — but three corrections. (1) refresh_cadence was recorded as "not stated"; the lookup page explicitly states it is updated nightly. (2) An earlier check missed a link on the same board page: "LLR Bulk License Verification" at https://eservice.llr.sc.gov/OnlineVerificationBulk. It is live (HTTP 200) and is a genuine bulk verification service, but it sits behind a username/password login with self-registration, so per the read-only ground rules I did not create an account and it cannot be scored as a free bulk file — bulk_file stays "paid". Worth flagging to whoever scopes SC, since a free account may turn SC into a Tier 1/2 source. (3) fields_present for SC should be treated as UNVERIFIED rather than observed: neither agent ever obtained a result row, because the search POST is rejected; status/issue_date/expiration_date/address are inferred from LLR's other LicLookup boards, not seen. I did not change those booleans since I could not disprove them either.

board_name: South Dakota Board of Pharmacy (SD Department of Health)
refresh_cadence: live system of record
portal_type: iGov Solutions / i3 Verticals (sdbop.igovsolution.net) - per-record business lookup, captcha-gated
notes: Everything else Confirmed, but fields_present.address=true is refuted and is internally inconsistent with an earlier check's own evidence: the agent quoted the result-grid headers as "Certification Type, Certification No #, Status, Orginal Date, Effective Date, Expiration Date" — which contains no address — yet still marked address=true. I dumped every <th> in the page and the grid is exactly those six columns, twice (two grid instances), with no Address, City, State, Zip or Business Name column at all. Address is only an INPUT to the search (txtcity, txt_zip), not an output. Since the captcha blocks reaching any detail view, address must be scored false/unverified. Practical consequence: even if someone solved the captcha, SD's grid yields no street address, which materially weakens it as a closure-monitoring source beyond what the claim implies.

board_name: Tennessee Board of Pharmacy (TN Dept. of Health, Health Related Boards)
format: html (full result set returned in one response)
refresh_cadence: daily; sibling app /LicensureReports states "Data last updated 08/14/2026"
portal_type: Custom TDH ASP.NET MVC app "FacilityListings" (not MyLicense/iGov/GLSuite/Accela/Salesforce/Pega)
notes: The headline claim is Confirmed and actually much stronger than stated — I replicated the single unauthenticated POST byte-for-byte (9,083,278 bytes, "Results = 7268") and the closed-pharmacy retention is far richer than the two examples given: of 7,268 rows, 3,553 Licensed, 2,935 "Facility Closed", 415 Expired, 197 "Closed Appl", 87 "Withdrew Appl", 47 "Appl in process", 9 Revoked, 9 "Admin Error", 6 Lapsed, 5 Denied, 2 "On Probation", 2 "Exp-Suspended", 1 Suspended. So retains_closed=yes is emphatic: ~40% of the roster is a dated-by-nothing but named "Facility Closed" record, which makes TN the strongest closure-history source in this batch alongside OK. One correction: history_public="yes" was asserted from the mere presence of the History Search form; I actually exercised it and it did not deliver. Two operational notes an earlier check missed: (a) the endpoint 403s plain curl and requires a browser User-Agent; (b) the token/cookie pair from the GET must be carried into the POST.
